description:
Overview

The Department of Political Science at the University of Oslo offers a PhD Research Fellow (SKO 1017) position within the POLIGROW project, “How Policy Growth Affects Policy Implementation and Performance”, funded by the Norwegian Research Council. The fellowship is fully funded and salaried, with no tuition.

The position is for three years, extendable to a maximum of four years to accommodate qualifying activities such as teaching. The expected start date is 1 April 2027, subject to negotiation.

The POLIGROW Project

The project studies how policy growth changes the administrative structures, working routines and performance of the authorities responsible for implementation. It is organised in three work packages: mapping implementation tasks across 15 OECD countries (1975–2025); examining bureaucrats’ coping practices through case studies and interviews; and analysing how patterns of burden allocation affect policy effectiveness.

The PhD fellow develops an independent project within this framework, using data generated by POLIGROW, and contributes to the collective data collection — especially Work Package I.

Funding and Terms

What the fellowship provides

Eligibility

  • Prior education corresponding to five years of university-level study in Norway in political science or a related field, including 120 ECTS at master’s level.
  • A master’s thesis equivalent to at least 30 ECTS (half a year of full-time study), with relevant training in research design and methods.
  • Excellent academic record, normally grades in the A–B range on the Norwegian A–F scale or equivalent.
  • Very good to excellent command of English, written and oral. Non-EU/EEA applicants without an English-native background or English-language MA must document TOEFL 550 PBT / 80 iBT or IELTS 6.0.
  • Robust empirical research knowledge with quantitative or qualitative proficiency; knowledge of German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese or a Scandinavian language is an advantage.

How to Apply

  • Submit the application through the Jobbnorge electronic recruitment system before 14 December 2026. Attachments must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
  • Include a cover letter (max. two pages) with a motivation statement, a research proposal (max. 3,000 words including references, with a word count on the front page), and a CV.
  • Attach a copy of the master’s thesis, transcripts (with thesis grade), an explanation of your grading system if foreign, and names/contact details of 2–3 referees.
  • Include English-test documentation if you are a non-EU/EEA applicant without an English-native background or English-language MA.
